items.title: 66960_Gil Evans oral history interview
items.q: I remember one time I took an arrangement up to a publisher ( for an album ?) called 'Easy Things to Remember'. Rodgers and Hart tune.

ctx.x: He said, only the worst kinds of people did. And that his mother positively forbade him to follow them. But of course, they were irresistible for him, you see. (LAUGHTER).

Sounds funny, but it's basically a fear of sexuality. All of it. I remember one time I took an arrangement up to a publisher ( for an album ?) called 'Easy Things to Remember'. Rodgers and Hart tune. 'Easy Things to Remember'. I had it written like this. (PLAYS PIANO). Kind of like this. (PLAYS PIANO).

He said, 'that's the dirtiest thing I ever heard. It reminds me,' this is a man from Boston, I was flabbergasted, he said, 'that's the dirtiest thing I ever heard. It reminds me of a dose of clap.' Up in Chapell Music. A big high class music company here in New York. This was twenty years ago.
